title: 4D530013-Blinx_The_Time_Sweeper.xiso.iso
prediction: RE-REGISTERED 2026-09-26 23:20Z, before any Thor arm has run: the first registration (71d7a1552b, MAX 2/3) was superseded when the Nova idle probe showed fan_mode 3 is not the fan's maximum (NOTES 5a). Nothing of the Thor's has been read since. THE PILOT for the gameplay regimen, registered before any arm has run and before `settings put` has been tried on either device. One HELD Thor session (docs/lanes/perfregimen/held_session.sh thor <dir>, under 30 min, >= 50% battery at start): an idle probe that steps performance_mode 0,1,2 and fan_mode 0,1,2,3,5 with no title running, then three hands-off 250 s Blinx arms through soak_title.sh at 60b49e304d in the order REST (0/4), MAX (2/5), REST. REST-MAX-REST, so that drift across the session (heat, battery) shows up as a difference between the two REST arms rather than being read as the mode's effect. The APK is whatever the dispatcher last installed on the Thor, the same in all three arms. The session records its versionName and the env pref. Judge: python3 docs/lanes/perfregimen/judge.py <dir> --prediction docs/testing/predictions/perfregimen-pilot-thor.json (fps = the median gfps=N value, 135-245 s from the arm's first hakuX line; on current APKs gfps= is a ~2 s window whose value is the fps, so the blinx372c 60-flips-per-line cadence reader does not apply, NOTES 5a). Legs, each with the world in which it fails: M0 the instrument: every arm has >= 15 gfps lines in the window, and its perf_regimen.json reads back the modes it asked for with perf_restored true. Otherwise VOID, not a result. P1 at idle, kgsl min_clock_mhz at performance_mode 2 exceeds the value at 0 (401 MHz on the Thor at 0 today; the Nova reads 550 at 1). It fails if no OEM service observes a `settings put`, so that the write lands only in the settings table. That is the brief's central worry. P2 at idle, the fan PWM duty (/sys/class/gpio5_pwm2/duty) at fan_mode 5 (FanState.SPORT) is >= the duty at every other mode probed. It fails if the fan write is not observed on the Thor, or if the Thor's fan curve differs from the Nova's. P3 under the title, the MAX arm's median GPU floor and fan duty both exceed each REST arm's. It fails if the load's own governor boost masks the mode. P4 the two REST arms' demo fps agree within 8%. If not, drift or noise is as large as the effect, and P5/P6 say nothing. P5 non-inferiority: MAX demo fps >= 0.97 x the mean REST fps. It fails if MAX costs frame rate, for example if a fixed high CPU floor takes thermal headroom from the GPU. P6 a GUESS, labelled as one: MAX >= 1.05 x REST. blinx372c found the demo bound by two surface-download finish waits per frame, which are latency, not clock, so the gain may be small. If P6 fails with P1-P5 passing, the regimen is sound and Blinx is simply not clock-bound on the Thor.
expect_note: Named rules read by docs/lanes/perfregimen/judge.py, not golden keys: a soak writes no captures and arms.sh skips soaks.
